summary: Request for built-in cloud database authentication support in Temporal Server for AWS RDS and GCP Cloud SQL using workload identity, eliminating the need to manage database credentials as secrets in cloud-managed Kubernetes environments.
userImpact: Users running Temporal in AWS EKS or GCP GKE must currently manage database credentials as secrets instead of using native workload identity features.
rootCause: Temporal Server lacks built-in support for cloud provider IAM authentication mechanisms; existing Connect hook is undocumented and impractical for most users.
proposedFix: Add cloudAuth configuration to SQL persistence settings supporting AWS RDS and GCP Cloud SQL with automatic token refresh based on cloud provider token lifetimes.
workaround: Undocumented Connect hook can be used but requires custom builds and maintenance of upstream merges.
keyQuote: Add built-in support for cloud database authentication in Temporal's SQL configuration
